title: Counting a Doubled Bit
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word, $p,r$ Boolean words, $b$ a bit, and $n$ a natural number, with $x=p\mathbin{++}[b,b]\mathbin{++}r$. Starting in state $0$ at the clamped input offset $|p|$, with a unary counter of length $n$ whose head is at $n$ and empty output, the suffix-extraction machine reaches after two steps state $0$ at the clamped offset $|p|+2$, with a unary counter of length $n+1$ whose head is at $n+1$ and empty output.
replaced:
Let $x$ be an input of the form $p$, followed by two copies of a bit $b$, followed
by a word $r$, and let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. From the counting state at offset $|p|$
with a unary counter of length $n$, counter head at $n$, and empty output, two
steps of the suffix extractor yield the counting state at offset $|p| + 2$ with
counter length $n + 1$ and counter head at $n + 1$; nothing is emitted.
